title: Crypto, Access, and Audit: Acceptance Runbook for Private/VPC Deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: produce a single, testable acceptance runbook that operationalizes Security & Compliance requirements (SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logging, KMS/HSM) for Private and VPC customers. This ticket consolidates ambiguous PRD items, defines pass/fail criteria for rollout gates, and lists the artifacts required for security and compliance sign-off. Scope: private control plane + on-prem install flows, tenant RBAC model, integration points for customer KMS/HSM, SSO via SAML2.0 and OIDC, audit log export and retention, and evidence collection. Out of scope: hosted API pricing, model runtime performance tuning, Dedicated capacity autoscaling mechanics. Goals: 1) Eliminate interpretation gaps between PM/Eng/Security by producing concrete tests and data artifacts; 2) Provide a checklist that QA and Security can execute; 3) Define rollback and mitigation steps for failed audits or regression tests.
background: Multiple PRDs referenced different levels of RBAC granularity and KMS options. Security requested hardened KMS integration with HSM-backed keys for FIPS requirements, while Engineering flagged integration surface and upgrade complexity. Compliance needs documented evidence (logs, access records) to support SOC2/ISO audits. This runbook pulls together previous PRDs and the security team's ask into executable acceptance items.
decision_log: 2025-02-13: Agreed to support both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed CMK; HSM endorsement only for customer-managed HSM via KMIP/PKCS#11 connectors.
2025-02-14: RBAC model will use a role+resource policy that maps to existing Redwood IAM primitives; scoping to tenant-scoped roles for initial rollout.
2025-02-17: SAML 2.0 will be first-class for enterprise SSO; OIDC will be supported in parity but shipped in a follow-up patch with separate tests.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Customer can configure SAML IdP in Private control plane and perform a full login flow; assertion mapping to RBAC roles verified by Security (test accounts for admin, operator, auditor).

RBAC: Tenant-level roles (admin, operator, developer, auditor) enforce route- and model-level permissions; negative tests validate least-privilege behavior (e.g., developer cannot access billing endpoints).

Audit logs: All control-plane actions (user auth events, role changes, key rotations, deployment rollouts) are logged with immutable append-only semantics and can be exported to customer ELK/S3 with configurable retention. Evidence: sample exported log set for three-week window.

KMS/HSM: Customer-managed KMS integrations must support envelope encryption for model artifacts and tokens; integration tests demonstrate successful key wrap/unwrap using a customer CMK and documented HSM-backed key option via KMIP.

Crypto key rotation: Automated rotation workflow for Redwood-managed keys and manual rotation path for customer-managed keys with preserved accessibility to previously encrypted artifacts. Test: rotate and decrypt older artifacts.
Telemetry & tracing: Token-level cost/latency traces obfuscated and retained per retention policy; audit reviewer can correlate an action to an authenticated principal within 60s of the event.

Compliance docs: Provide an evidence bundle (configuration screenshots, exported logs, test run results, PR/merge links, and security review signoff) that satisfies SOC2 readiness checklist items mapped in this ticket.
test_plan: Environment: deploy a staging Private control plane behind a customer VPC with a mock SAML IdP and a KMIP-compatible HSM simulator.
SSO tests: create IdP metadata, configure assertion mappings, perform login SAML flow for three roles and capture SAML assertions and session tokens.
RBAC tests: run a matrix of API calls for each role; assert HTTP 200 for allowed calls and 403 for forbidden; capture audit entries.
Audit export: configure log export to S3, run retention pruning job, and confirm export file integrity and schema conformity.
KMS tests: encrypt a model artifact using envelope encryption, rotate the underlying CMK, verify decryptability post-rotation.
Failure injection: simulate key unavailability and confirm graceful error messages and fallback guidance for operators.
runbook: Pre-merge checklist: security design review completed, threat model updated, test harness and mock IdP/HSM integrated into CI.
Pre-deploy gating: automated RBAC matrix tests passing, audit export verified, KMS integration smoke tests green.
Deployment: feature flags enabled per-tenant; incremental rollout via canary to single-customer staging then to pilot cohort.
Post-deploy validation: execute acceptance test matrix against canary tenants and collect evidence package.
Rollback criteria: any privacy or crypto regression (inability to decrypt archived artifacts) -> immediate rollback to previous release and incident trigger.
acceptance_checklist: Design review doc linked and acked by Security and Infra leads.
SSO smoke flow (admin/operator/auditor) proof-of-login artifacts attached.
RBAC matrix results attached (CSV) showing allowed/denied matrix.
Audit export sample (3 weeks) attached to evidence bundle and validated schema.
KMS integration test logs demonstrating wrap/unwrap and rotation success.
CI test coverage >=70% for new RBAC and KMS code paths.
Security review approval and signed risk exceptions (if any).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: HSM compatibility matrix is broad and vendor APIs vary. Mitigation: support generic KMIP and publish tested vendor list; provide fallbacks for unsupported vendors.
Risk: Misconfigured SAML assertions can map users to incorrect roles. Mitigation: create assertion validation tool in control plane and include mapping preview before activation.
Risk: Audit log volume could be large and increase storage costs. Mitigation: configurable retention with tiered export; sample retention policies provided to customers.
